predecessors.name: Kingdom of Castile
predecessors.text: Castile, united for good with León in 1230

successors.name: Kingdom of Spain
successors.text: the Crown of Castile (with Granada, the Canaries, the Indies and Navarre), whose throne Charles took in 1516

ledger.x: 1236: Ferdinand III takes Córdoba; Castile and León, united for good in 1230, are drawn as the Crown of Castile.
1236: Córdoba is conquered.
1238: Niebla and Huelva come under Castile as a client.
1243: Murcia and Orihuela accept Castilian protection by the pact of Alcaraz.
1244: Ferdinand III captures Arjona.
1246: Jaén surrenders under the Treaty of Jaén (March 1246).
1246: Granada becomes Ferdinand III's vassal.
1248: Ferdinand III enters Seville on 22 December.
1261: Alfonso X captures Jerez.
ledger.cp: Muslim rulers of Jerez (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1262: Niebla's client status ends in annexation ('Niebla in 1262' absorbed).
1262: Alfonso X annexes Niebla.
1264: the Mudéjar revolt breaks out.
1266: the revolt and the Aragonese interlude end; Murcia returns to Castile.
1266: the protectorate of Murcia ends.
1266: the Kingdom of Murcia is annexed by Castile ('Annexed by Castile: 1266'); Alicante's absorption is dated 1266 on the Ferdinand III page.
1292: Castile captures Tarifa in October 1292 and keeps it.
1296: Aragon invades the Kingdom of Murcia.

1304: the Treaty of Torrellas (9 August 1304) awards Aragon 'many cities north of the Segura'; Castile is 'restored' the Kingdom of Murcia except the part conquered earlier, and James retained a portion of Villena.
1305: the border is finalised, 'the following year' (Treaty of Elche).
1309: Castile takes Gibraltar.
1327: Alfonso XI takes Olvera and its neighbours from Granada.
1330: Alfonso XI takes Teba.
1333: the Marinids retake Gibraltar.
1342: Castile captures Priego and Alcalá la Real.
1344: Algeciras surrenders after the siege begun on 3 August 1342.
1357: Castile penetrates Aragon and conquers Tarazona on 9 March; truce arranged on 8 May.
1361: the peace of Terrer (18 May 1361): conquered places and castles were returned to their original lords.
1363: Castile again occupies Tarazona and takes Cariñena, Teruel, Segorbe, Morvedre, Almenara, Xiva and Bunyol, and in Valencia 'Alicante, Caudete, Elda, Gandia, and other places'.
1369: the war ends with Peter's fall: 'The war lasted from 1356 to 1369, prolonged because Peter of Castile lost his throne to Henry of Trastámara.'
1369: Muhammad V of Granada recaptures Algeciras from Castile.
1370: Biscay joins the Crown.
1402: Jean de Béthencourt and Gadifer de la Salle land on Lanzarote 'in the summer of 1402'.
1405: Fuerteventura ('The conquest of the island was completed in 1405 with the surrender of the native kings') and El Hierro ('took place in 1405') are taken.
1407: Zahara passes to Castile.
1410: Ferdinand, co-regent of Castile, conquers Antequera, whence his surname.
1462: a small Castilian force led by Alonso de Arcos, governor of Tarifa, takes Gibraltar; the garrison surrenders to Juan Alonso, 'now the first Duke of Medina Sidonia'.
1481: Granada seizes Zahara.
1482: La Gomera appears in Cliopatria's Castile shape.
1482: the Granada War begins with Alhama.
1482: the tribute that kept Granada a vassal stops with the war.
1482: Castile takes Alhama de Granada; reinforcements on 28 April averted its retaking and Ferdinand took command there on 14 May 1482.
1483: Castile retakes Zahara.
1483: Gran Canaria is won.
1485: Ronda 'fell to him after fifteen days' and 'Ronda's fall allowed Marbella... to come into Christian hands next' (1485).
1486: Loja falls after a 'second Loja siege'; the page names the siege year, not the surrender.
1487: Vélez-Málaga capitulates on 27 April.
1487: Málaga falls on 18 August after a siege that began on 7 May.
1487: the western campaign ends with Málaga on 18 August 1487.
1489: Castile besieges Baza; the siege began in 1489 and, 'after six months, al-Zagal surrendered'.
1489: Baza surrenders to Castile after six months.
1489: Almería and Guadix surrender through al-Zagal.
1489: the eastern campaign is treated as ended with the surrenders; bridging judgment, the page gives no end date for it.
1491: the siege of Granada begins.
1492: Granada surrenders.
1492: the Granada War ends on 2 January.
1493: La Palma is won.
1496: Santo Domingo is founded.
1496: Tenerife is won.
1497: Melilla is conquered.
1502: Cliopatria adds 22 cells of western Hispaniola.
1505: the Spanish take Mers el-Kebir.
1508: Juan Ponce de León conquers Puerto Rico.
1509: the Spanish take Oran.
1509: the first Spanish settlement on Jamaica.
1510: Santa María la Antigua del Darién is settled, the first mainland settlement (Castilla de Oro); 'In 1513, Balboa crossed the Isthmus of Panama'.
1510: Cliopatria's 1512 shape holds the Béjaïa coast and Tripoli.
1511: Spanish settlement of eastern Cuba begins.
1512: Castile conquers Navarre.
1515: the Crown of Castile passes into the Spanish monarchy.

wars.name: Reconquest campaigns of Ferdinand III
wars.outcome: Córdoba (1236), Murcia by the pact of Alcaraz (1243), Arjona (1244), Jaén (March 1246) and Seville (22 December 1248) pass to Castile; Granada becomes a vassal.

wars.name: Mudéjar revolt of 1264-1266
wars.outcome: The revolt was put down; Aragon conquered Murcia and returned it to Castile; annexed 1266.

wars.name: Aragonese invasion of Murcia and the Treaty of Torrellas
wars.outcome: Aragon conquered Murcia between 1296 and 1301; the Treaty of Torrellas of 9 August 1304 awarded Aragon many cities north of the Segura and restored the rest of the Kingdom of Murcia to Castile; border finalised in 1305.

wars.name: Siege of Algeciras (1342-1344)
wars.outcome: Algeciras surrendered on 26 March 1344; Priego and Alcalá la Real fell in 1342 (Emirate page); ten-year truce and a tribute of twelve thousand doubloons from Granada.

wars.name: War of the Two Peters
wars.outcome: Castile occupied Tarazona (1357, 1363) and, in 1363, Cariñena, Teruel, Segorbe, Morvedre and Alicante; the peaces of Terrer (18 May 1361) and Morvedre (2 July 1363) did not end it; it ended with Peter's death at Montiel in 1369.

wars.name: Castilian-Granadan war of 1405-1410
wars.outcome: Ferdinand of Antequera conquered Antequera in 1410.

wars.name: Conquest of the Canary Islands
wars.outcome: Béthencourt took Lanzarote (1402), Fuerteventura and El Hierro (1405); the Crown conquered Gran Canaria (surrender 29 April 1483), La Palma (3 May 1493) and Tenerife (25 July 1496).

wars.name: Granada War
wars.outcome: Castilian-Aragonese victory: Alhama (1482), Ronda and Marbella (1485), Loja (1486), Vélez-Málaga and Málaga (1487), Baza and the east (1489), the Treaty of Granada (25 November 1491) and the surrender on 2 January 1492.

wars.name: War of the Castilian Succession
wars.outcome: Isabella and Ferdinand prevailed; the Crown page dates the war's end to 1479, the year of the personal union of the crowns.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of North African posts
wars.outcome: Several towns and outposts on the North African coast were conquered and occupied by Castile between 1505 and 1510; Melilla in 1497.

wars.name: Conquest of Navarre
wars.outcome: Castile conquered Navarre in 1512 and annexed it in 1515 (Crown page); the Spanish Empire page dates the conquest 1512-1529.

certainty.note: The Muslim and Portuguese frontiers are approximate and moved by sieges.
